messages.author: d588a03e58ea7e7f
messages.subject: Re: New theme system
parts:
On 5/28/2012 10:07 PM, Winston Chang wrote:
> Hi everyone -
>
> I've been working on the new theme system, based off the ideas Hadley
> posted a while back. I think it's to the point where it's ready for some
> feedback. Check it out and let me know if you have any comments or
> suggestions:
> https://github.com/wch/ggplot2/wiki/New-theme-system
>
> -Winston
>

I've just read the wiki page; I haven't looked at the code or even tried
installing it (yet). But I wanted to give some feedback:


The first thing, which I was VERY happy to see, was that you have a
backwards compatibility layer with deprecation messages. Hopefully the
message will point to the new (element_) function as well as a
transition-guide like resource (even that wiki page would be good).


I also like the element_*() renaming; the theme prefix meant two
different things, and that confusion has been eliminated.


I know that inheritance and single attribute updating were important
goals for the new design, so it is good to see that in there. A nice way
of specifying relative sizes is a nice addition. Gaining independent
control over x and y axis attributes is good. Perhaps that can be
further extended by having separate x/y versions of axis.ticks,
axis.ticks.length, axis.ticks.margin, and axis.line.


I am also glad that the implementation was not the start of the
description and that (it seems) the requirement drove the
implementation, and not the implementation driving the requirements.


Does rel() work only with font sizes, or could it (does it) work with
any numerical size. I'm thinking in particular margin/padding. Or any unit.


In terms of the inheritance structure:
* could legend.text and legend.title both inherit off of something off
of text? The obvious name would be legend.text, but that doesn't work
here since it is already being used.
* Can the margins (legend.margin, panel.margin, axis.ticks.margin,
plot.margin) inherit off a single margin, and maybe even use rel?
* Should there be some sort of relationship between segment and line?
They both have colour, size, and linetype. I'm thinking segment
inherits from line.
* There are two align's and a justification (legend.justification,
legend.title.align, legend.text.align). I'm not sure what each take and
whether they could be related (in an inheritance way) to each other.
* What is the difference between legend.direction and legend.box? Both
take "horizontal" or "vertical" as values.
* Should the title text really be part of the theme? As I think about
the themes, it seems like it shouldn't. If not, then there is the
problem of where to put it. It is most similar to the labels of the
scales, but it is really not a scale. Short of just making a dedicated
function for it, or just putting it into labs(), I'm not sure what to do
with it.
* The only other elements that don't inherit from anything are:
axis.ticks.length, legend.position, title, legend.direction, legend.box.
I think that is fine; the first is a unit, but doesn't really relate to
anything; maybe to the margin sizes if that becomes a set. The three
legend bits are their own thing, and title is just a string.


Is precedence well defined for things like:

opts(axis.text = element_text(size=rel(0.5)),
axis.text = element_text(size=4))

That is, will it work and will it give a consistent result?


Rather than modifying a theme directly as a list, why not utilize the
existing opts() infrastructure for assignment? or update?

mytheme <- theme_grey()

mytheme <- update(mytheme, opts(text = element_text(family="Times",
face="plain", colour="red", size=16, hjust=0.5, vjust=0.5, angle=0,
lineheight=0.9)))

or maybe

mytheme <- opts(text = element_text(family="Times", face="plain",
colour="red", size=16, hjust=0.5, vjust=0.5, angle=0, lineheight=0.9))

although the latter would have to either specify everything or fall back
to some defaults for unspecified things.
The advantage of this approach is that it insulates the implementation,
which isn't too hard since there already exists a way of specifying the
structure (using element_*) independent of the implementation.


How deep does relative sizing work? For instance:

opts(text = element_text(size=16),
axis.text = element_text(size=rel(0.5)),
axis.text.x = element_text(size=rel(0.25)))

What would the size of the text on the x axis be? 16*0.5*0.25=2 (rel's
are multiplicative up the tree)? 16*0.5=8 (only the first rel going down
the tree matters and any subsequent ones are ignored)? 16*0.25=4 (only
the last rel in the tree matters, and it is in reference to the last
absolute value)? I think the first one is what it should be.


In general, I really like the new design. I think it fixes many problems
of the old one, and I don't see any glaringly obvious problems with it.

--
Brian S. Diggs, PhD
Senior Research Associate, Department of Surgery
Oregon Health & Science University

messages.author: d31339b95f6e694c
messages.subject: Re: New theme system
parts:
On 2012-May-29, at 20:03 , Brian Diggs wrote:
>
> Rather than modifying a theme directly as a list, why not utilize the existing opts() infrastructure for assignment? or update?

Personally, I really like the ability to be able to modify the theme as a list: it uses common knowledge, does not require to learn new functions, is quite explicit, if it could work with the base elements (like theme_grey$text$size = 12) it allows to affect much of the plot aspect in a single assignment etc.

For what it's worth, I would argue that this should be the only interface if that was possible, or at least the interface of choice.

Jean-Olivier Irisson

>> Rather than modifying a theme directly as a list, why not utilize the existing opts() infrastructure for assignment? or update?

> Personally, I really like the ability to be able to modify the theme as a list: it uses common knowledge, does not require to learn new functions, is quite explicit, if it could work with the base elements (like theme_grey$text$size = 12) it allows to affect much of the plot aspect in a single assignment etc.

The disadvantage is that it's difficult to document, and you get
errors late - when the plot is rendered, not when you modify the
theme.
